## Plan: Immediate Detailed Weather and Pro Calendar Dashboard

Implement two related improvements without changing the non-Pro navigation model: make a newly enabled detailed-weather preference invalidate an incompatible current-weather cache immediately, and replace the existing Pro calendar page with the complete dashboard shown in the concept image. The dashboard will be a responsive landscape two-column / portrait stacked page, use the existing clock preferences and QWeather configuration, obtain current plus three-day weather online, and resolve Chinese festivals, solar terms, and official holiday/workday markers from pinned offline calendar assets. Use Apple's China mainland holiday iCalendar feed as the primary festival/solar-term source and retain `holiday-cn` as a complementary source for official rest/work status.

### Confirmed scope and product decisions

- Modify the existing Pro `月历` page only. Compat and Modern keep their current screens and navigation, but the shared detailed-weather bug fix must work in all three flavors.
- Reproduce the complete concept screen, not only its right calendar panel. Landscape uses left time/weather cards and right month calendar; portrait stacks the same modules and may scroll when needed.
- The three-day forecast follows the master `显示实时天气` switch. It does not depend on `显示详细天气信息`; the latter continues to control only the extra current-weather carousel on clock pages.
- Bundle a pinned snapshot of `https://calendars.icloud.com/holidays/cn_zh.ics` as the primary festival and solar-term data source. Also bundle `holiday-cn` data for 2025, 2026, and 2027 as a complementary official `休`/`班` source and consistency check. Dates outside packaged official-arrangement coverage still show Gregorian, lunar, festival, and solar-term information when present in the ICS snapshot, but must not invent `休`/`班` markers.
- Preserve the existing Pro bottom navigation. The concept design applies to the content area above it.

### Concept-image analysis and target visual specification

- The reference is a 1365 x 768 landscape composition with an approximately 50/50 split: a left dashboard column around 673 px wide, an 8-10 px gutter, and a right calendar panel around 665 px wide. The outer margin and inter-card gutters are about 10 px.
- Use a near-black page background and medium charcoal panels with small corner radii (approximately 8-12 dp after density-independent adaptation). There are no borders or shadows. Primary text is near-white, secondary text is light gray, inactive adjacent-month text is muted gray, active informational accents are vivid blue, off-day accents are green, and make-up-workday accents are amber/yellow.
- Left column, top card: compact network/battery status at top-left; a very large heavy-weight `HH:mm` time; smaller blue `:ss` aligned to the main time baseline. Respect the app's 12/24-hour, seconds, small-seconds, bold, font family, time color, and app time-zone preferences where practical.
- Left column, middle card: large current-weather icon at left; current temperature as the dominant value; `体感温度` plus feels-like temperature to its right; a bottom line containing location, weather condition, daytime wind direction/scale, and humidity. Use blue for icon, selected location segment, and feels-like value, with neutral text elsewhere.
- Left column, bottom card: three equal columns labeled `今天`, `明天`, `后天`; each contains the QWeather day icon, day condition, and `min - max ℃`. The concept shows blue emphasis for today and neutral white/gray for later days.
- Right card: centered `yyyy 年 M 月` title; Sunday-first weekday headings; a fixed 7 x 6 month grid; each cell shows a large Gregorian day and a fixed-height secondary label area. With no festival or solar term, that area statically shows the short lunar date. If the date has at least one festival or solar term, it vertically cycles through the short lunar date and every festival/solar-term name using an upward slide transition modeled on the detailed-weather carousel. Adjacent-month days remain visible at reduced opacity. The current date is green. Official off-days display a small green `休`; official make-up workdays display an amber `班`.
- Right-card footer: selected Gregorian date, blue weekday, and natural Chinese lunar date such as `壬寅虎年三月廿六`. Default selection is today. Tapping a day updates the footer. The entire month calendar panel must support direct horizontal paging: swipe left to the next month and swipe right to the previous month. Keep accessible previous/next icon controls as equivalent alternatives; tapping the month title or a dedicated accessibility action returns to today. Controls may be visually subdued so the title remains close to the concept.
- Responsive behavior: add a landscape-specific layout with weighted left/right columns and a portrait/default layout that stacks modules. Use stable min heights, weights, and text-size resource variants instead of viewport-based font scaling. On compact portrait screens, place content in a `NestedScrollView`; never allow the calendar grid, forecast labels, or navigation to overlap.

### Root cause and detailed-weather fix

1. In `WeatherController.start(int)`, the controller emits any matching location cache and calls `refreshIfNeeded(cached, false)`. The latter skips the network while `updatedAt` is inside the configured interval.
2. A cache created while detailed weather was disabled has `WeatherDisplayData.detail == null`. Applying settings calls `startWeatherIfEnabled()` in both `MainActivity` and `ProClockFragment`, but the fresh basic cache is considered valid, so no request occurs until expiry or a location change forces one.
3. Introduce an explicit cache-capability check owned by the weather domain, for example `WeatherDisplayData.satisfies(boolean detailedRequired)` or a package-visible/static `WeatherController.isCacheCompatible(...)`. A cache is compatible only when it matches the existing source/location rules and, when `ClockPreferences.isWeatherDetailed()` is true, has non-null detail data. Do not infer compatibility from timestamps alone.
4. In `start`, it is acceptable to emit the basic cached current weather immediately to avoid blanking the UI, but call `refreshIfNeeded` with a forced refresh when the cache lacks required detail. The forced path must bypass only the age test, not permissions, location-mode validation, configuration checks, generation cancellation, or error handling.
5. Preserve normal cache reuse when detailed weather changes from enabled to disabled; detailed data is a superset and does not need a network request. Repeated Apply actions with no relevant preference change must not create redundant fetches.
6. Keep the existing settings callbacks. Both flavor-specific `SettingsDialog.applySelection()` implementations already save `weatherDetailed` before notifying their listener, and both host paths restart the controller after Apply. Verify this order rather than adding a second UI-specific refresh mechanism.

### Weather data design

1. Add immutable daily models under `WeatherModels`, such as `DailyForecast` (`fxDate`, `tempMin`, `tempMax`, `iconDay`, `textDay`, optional day wind/humidity fields) and `DailyForecastData` (`locationId`, location labels, `updatedAt`, ordered entries, and QWeather attribution metadata if retained).
2. Extend `QWeatherClient` with a focused daily call using `GET /v7/weather/3d?location={LocationID-or-lon,lat}&lang=zh`. Reuse `request`, JWT signing, API host, timeout, TLS compatibility, error-code handling, and URL encoding. Parse by `fxDate`; never assume array index 0 is today. Required display fields are `fxDate`, `tempMin`, `tempMax`, `iconDay`, and `textDay`; retain `windDirDay`, `windScaleDay`, and `humidity` if the middle current-weather line will use forecast fallback.
3. Do not repeat the QWeather location policy inconsistently. For manual mode use the saved LocationID and saved city/district labels. For automatic mode resolve the coordinates through the existing GeoAPI flow, then use the resolved LocationID and labels. If extracting a small shared location-resolution helper removes duplication between current and daily clients, keep it package-private and narrowly scoped.
4. Add a separate `DailyForecastRepository` SharedPreferences cache keyed by location source plus manual LocationID. Serialize the three entries structurally with `JSONObject`/`JSONArray`. A cache is reusable only if it contains entries for the device/app-zone current date, tomorrow, and the day after tomorrow.
5. Add a lifecycle-aware `DailyForecastController` modeled on `WeatherController`: generation tokens, one executor, main-thread delivery, location permission handling, manual/automatic modes, cancellation in `stop`, and `shutdown`. Use a forecast cache TTL no longer than six hours and force expiry at local midnight, consistent with QWeather's 1-6 hour daily-forecast caching guidance. Expose loading/success/error states so the calendar can show cached data, progress, and a compact offline/error fallback.
6. The Pro calendar fragment may own one existing `WeatherController` for current conditions and one `DailyForecastController` for the forecast. Start both only while the view is resumed and the master weather switch is enabled; stop both in `onPause`, shut them down in `onDestroyView`, and avoid updating detached views. Do not fetch weather merely because the user browses another month.
7. When weather is disabled, hide the QWeather-derived current and forecast content or show a restrained local placeholder while retaining the time and calendar. Do not request location or network. When permission/config/network fails, retain non-expired cached data if available and expose a concise status rather than collapsing the card.
8. Add a visible, separately placed `天气服务由和风天气驱动` attribution within the calendar dashboard whenever QWeather data is displayed; make it open `https://www.qweather.com`. The existing attribution implementation/logo can be reused. Preserve `refer.sources` if warning or air-quality data is shown on this page, because QWeather requires those sources to be displayed unmodified.

### Calendar events, solar terms, and offline holiday design

1. Download and pin the raw iCloud feed from `https://calendars.icloud.com/holidays/cn_zh.ics` at implementation time, store it unmodified at `app/src/pro/assets/calendar/cn_zh.ics`, and record the retrieval date plus a SHA-256 digest in a neighboring provenance file. The feed inspected on 2026-07-28 contained 246 `VEVENT` records spanning explicit start years 2023-2029, all 24 solar terms in each year from 2024 through 2029, traditional festivals, fixed-date observances, yearly recurrence rules, and published `（休）`/`（班）` arrangements for 2024-2026. Treat this as a snapshot, not as a guarantee that future downloads have identical coverage.
2. Keep `app/src/pro/assets/holidays/2025.json`, `2026.json`, and `2027.json` from `holiday-cn`, plus its MIT license at `app/src/pro/assets/licenses/holiday-cn-LICENSE.txt`. Record the exact upstream release/commit. The iCloud snapshot is the primary source for names and solar terms; `holiday-cn` supplements and validates official rest/work status, especially when the ICS snapshot has no published arrangement for a year. Never infer future official days off from ordinary festivals.
3. Add an `IcsCalendarRepository` under the calendar package. Prefer a vetted Android-compatible RFC 5545 parser; if dependency compatibility or size is unacceptable, implement only the feed's required subset behind this repository and test it rigorously. At minimum, support UTF-8, CRLF/LF input, RFC line unfolding (continuation lines beginning with space or tab), property parameters such as `VALUE=DATE` and `LANGUAGE=zh_CN`, escaped text, `VEVENT`, `UID`, all-day `DTSTART`/`DTEND`, `SUMMARY`, `RRULE`, `CATEGORIES`, and `X-APPLE-SPECIAL-DAY`. Ignore unknown properties safely.
4. Interpret all-day `DTEND` as exclusive. Expand a multi-day `SUMMARY` ending in `（休）` across `DTSTART <= date < DTEND`, creating an off-day marker for every covered date. Treat a `（班）` event as a make-up-workday marker. Expand the feed's supported yearly rules such as `FREQ=YEARLY;COUNT=6` within the snapshot's bounded date range. Do not implement unbounded recurrence or perform network access at runtime.
5. Normalize each ICS event into an immutable model with `date`, canonical display name, event kind (`SOLAR_TERM`, `TRADITIONAL_FESTIVAL`, `FIXED_OBSERVANCE`, `OFF_DAY`, or `WORK_DAY`), source UID, and source priority. Strip only the terminal `（休）`/`（班）` status suffix after recording its meaning. Status-only events contribute badges and should not duplicate a same-date canonical festival label. Deduplicate equal normalized names on the same date while preserving distinct events, for example both `立春` and `春节`.
6. Add `HolidayRepository` for `holiday-cn`. Parse JSON with `org.json` into an immutable ISO-date map containing `name`, `date`, and `isOffDay`. Load all bundled files, let the later source-year file win on duplicate dates, and fail closed on malformed/missing assets. Merge status with this precedence: an explicit `holiday-cn` record wins; otherwise use explicit ICS `（休）`/`（班）`; otherwise no badge. Log or expose a test failure for conflicting sources rather than silently converting ordinary weekends into holidays.
7. Extend `CalendarMonth.Day` or compose it into `CalendarDayPresentation` with an ISO/local date key, short lunar label, ordered calendar-event labels, and merged holiday status. Keep the pure 42-cell month calculation independent from Android APIs. Replace the earlier proposal to calculate or hard-code solar terms/festivals locally: use the pinned ICS for those labels, with the existing lunar calculation retained only for lunar-date text and long footer formatting.
8. Add a reusable fixed-height `CalendarLabelCarouselView` (or an equivalent lightweight custom renderer) for the secondary line in every day cell. Its item order is always short lunar date first, followed by all distinct event labels in deterministic source order. If there are no event labels, render the lunar date statically and schedule no animation. If at least one event exists, cycle indefinitely through `[lunar date, event 1, event 2, ...]`.
9. Match the detailed-weather motion language: hold each settled item for approximately 3000 ms, then move the current label upward while the next label enters from below over approximately 200 ms. Clip drawing to the label viewport, keep its measured width/height constant throughout transitions, use monotonic uptime, and pause/remove callbacks when the fragment is not resumed or the cell is detached. A shared frame ticker owned by the calendar grid is preferable to 42 independent perpetual animators; stagger deterministic per-cell phases if simultaneous movement is visually noisy. Do not horizontally marquee short calendar labels.
10. Carousel accessibility must expose one stable description containing the lunar date plus all festival/solar-term names, and must not announce every automatic transition. Respect the system animator-duration/Remove Animations setting: when animations are disabled, show a deterministic static event label while retaining the full accessibility description. Rendering rules remain: `休` is green, `班` is amber, today is green, selection has a separate accessible treatment, and adjacent-month opacity must not make badges illegible.
11. Add a natural long lunar formatter for the footer (`sexagenary stem/branch + zodiac + 年 + lunar month/day`) without the square brackets currently emitted by `LunarCalendar.format`. Keep the existing formatter unchanged for clock-screen compatibility and add a new method. Include lunar text, all event names, work status, and selected/today state in each day cell's content description.

### Horizontal month paging behavior

1. Treat the right-hand calendar panel as a horizontally pageable month surface. A leftward swipe advances exactly one calendar month; a rightward swipe moves back exactly one calendar month. Paging must work from any point inside the month grid that is not already consumed by an accessibility control, and it must work in both landscape and portrait layouts.
2. Prefer a bounded three-page implementation (previous/current/next month) using a nested horizontal pager or an equivalent custom page container. After a completed transition, recenter/rebind the three pages around the new visible month so users can continue swiping indefinitely without allocating one page per month. Do not place another `ViewPager2` directly inside the existing vertical Pro `ViewPager2` without explicit nested-scroll arbitration; if a nested pager is used, the month pager must receive predominantly horizontal gestures while the outer app pager/navigation behavior remains stable.
3. The drag should be visually direct and track the finger. During a swipe, the outgoing month and adjacent incoming month move horizontally together with no fade-only replacement. Complete the page change when horizontal displacement exceeds roughly 25% of the calendar-panel width or horizontal fling velocity exceeds the platform minimum fling threshold; otherwise animate back to the current month. Use the platform touch slop and velocity tracker rather than raw pixel constants.
4. Lock gesture direction only after movement exceeds touch slop. Claim the gesture as month paging when `abs(deltaX) > abs(deltaY)` by a clear bias such as 1.2; otherwise leave it to the portrait `NestedScrollView`. Once direction is locked, do not switch axes mid-gesture. A short movement within touch slop remains a day-cell tap, so horizontal paging must not make date selection unreliable.
5. Keep the month title, 42 cells, holiday badges, lunar/event carousels, and selected-date footer synchronized with the settled page. Prepare adjacent month pages before they become visible so there is no blank frame. Pause label carousels on pages that are not settled/current; after paging completes, release stale callbacks and start only the newly visible month's carousels.
6. Selection behavior must be deterministic. When paging to another month, select the same day-of-month when it exists, clamped to the destination month's last day when necessary, and update the footer immediately after settling. Returning to today selects today and recenters the pager. Tapping an adjacent-month date displayed in the current 6-week grid selects that date and animates to its owning month using the same paging transition.
7. Previous/next buttons, keyboard/D-pad actions, accessibility scroll-forward/scroll-backward actions, and horizontal swipes must call the same month-navigation method so state restoration and animation behavior cannot diverge. Announce the newly settled `yyyy年M月` once for accessibility, but do not announce intermediate drag states.
8. Leaving the Pro calendar page is a session boundary for month browsing. If the user has paged to any other month, then switches to another Pro page such as Clock, Alarm, Timer, or Stopwatch and later returns to Calendar, reset the calendar to the month containing the current app-zone date, select today, update the footer to today, recenter the previous/current/next page set, and restart only today's visible label carousels. The return reset should happen immediately without replaying every intervening month animation.
9. Distinguish a real page switch from an in-place lifecycle interruption. A transient pause, settings dialog, permission dialog, app background/foreground cycle, or configuration recreation while Calendar remains the selected Pro destination must not be treated as navigation away. Preserve the settled visible year/month and selected date for those cases. Have `ProMainActivity`/the pager's `onPageSelected` callback explicitly notify the calendar fragment when its navigation destination is left and re-entered rather than relying only on `onPause()`/`onResume()`, because those lifecycle callbacks can also occur for dialogs, backgrounding, and recreation.
10. Respect reduced-motion settings. When animator duration is disabled, preserve the same gesture and state semantics but settle immediately after release. Save only the settled visible year/month and selected date, never an in-progress drag offset. Restore that saved state only when Calendar remained the selected destination across recreation; if Calendar was left for another Pro destination, the return-to-today rule takes precedence over saved browsing state.

### Layout and UI implementation sequence

1. Refactor `fragment_pro_calendar.xml` into the portrait/stacked dashboard shell and add `app/src/pro/res/layout-land/fragment_pro_calendar.xml` for the two-column concept layout. Extract repeated cards into included layouts only if this materially reduces duplication; do not nest decorative cards.
2. Add small shape/color/dimension resources in Pro resources for panel backgrounds, selection/today treatment, landscape/portrait typography, gutters, and stable card/grid dimensions. Keep user-selected background/time/date colors where the existing preferences define them, while retaining semantic blue/green/amber accents with sufficient contrast.
3. Implement a reusable public `WeatherIconView` in `com.clockmods.ui` that delegates to the existing package-private `WeatherIcon` SVG asset loader. This lets XML/fragment views render existing QWeather icon assets without duplicating SVG parsing or exposing mutable drawing details.
4. In `ProCalendarFragment`, bind the modular views, update the time once per second with a main-thread runnable, reuse `StatusBarView`, and apply `ClockTypefaceResolver`/clock preferences consistently. Remove callbacks in `onPause`/`onDestroyView`.
5. Bind current-weather state to the middle card and daily state to the three forecast columns. Map forecasts by local ISO date and format temperatures robustly when a field is absent. Keep all user-facing text in resources.
6. Rework month rendering to bind 42 stable day cells, merged holiday badges, per-cell lunar/event carousel items, selection, and footer text. The grid must own or coordinate carousel timing so recycled/rebound cells cannot retain stale dates or callbacks. Preserve visible month/selection through in-place recreation only; when the user leaves Calendar for another Pro destination, discard that browsing session so re-entry resets to today.
7. Implement the horizontally pageable previous/current/next month surface described above, including finger-tracking translation, distance/velocity completion thresholds, snap-back, axis locking, adjacent-page prebinding, and synchronization of title, selection, footer, and label-carousels. Retain 48 dp accessible targets for previous/next/today actions, heading semantics for the month title, and equivalent accessibility scroll actions.
8. Refresh calendar page preferences when Settings Apply is invoked. `ProMainActivity` currently refreshes only the clock fragment, so add a narrowly scoped adapter/activity dispatch that asks the existing calendar fragment to rebind weather enabled state, fonts/colors/time zone, and controller lifecycle without recreating the whole pager.
9. In `ProMainActivity`'s existing page-selection callback, track the previous and newly selected Pro destinations. Notify the calendar page explicitly when it is exited and entered. On genuine re-entry after another destination, call one idempotent calendar method that resets visible month and selection to the current app-zone date, rebinds the three month pages/title/footer, and restarts visible-page carousels. Do not trigger this reset when merely reopening Settings over the calendar, backgrounding the app, rotating/recreating the activity with Calendar still selected, or reselecting Calendar without having visited another destination.

### Relevant files

- `app/src/main/java/com/clockmods/weather/WeatherController.java` — enforce cache capability when detailed weather is required.
- `app/src/main/java/com/clockmods/weather/WeatherModels.java` — cache-compatibility helper and daily forecast/state models.
- `app/src/main/java/com/clockmods/weather/QWeatherClient.java` — daily forecast endpoint and parsing, reusing JWT/TLS/request infrastructure.
- `app/src/main/java/com/clockmods/weather/WeatherRepository.java` — preserve current-weather detail serialization; optionally expose/test cache capability at the correct layer.
- `app/src/main/java/com/clockmods/weather/DailyForecastController.java` — new lifecycle/location/fetch coordinator.
- `app/src/main/java/com/clockmods/weather/DailyForecastRepository.java` — new structured forecast cache.
- `app/src/main/java/com/clockmods/ui/WeatherIcon.java` and `app/src/main/java/com/clockmods/ui/WeatherIconView.java` — reuse packaged QWeather SVG icons from regular views.
- `app/src/main/java/com/clockmods/calendar/CalendarMonth.java` — date identity/presentation support while retaining the six-week grid.
- `app/src/main/java/com/clockmods/calendar/LunarCalendar.java` — natural footer format; keep existing APIs backward compatible.
- `app/src/main/java/com/clockmods/calendar/IcsCalendarRepository.java`, `CalendarEvent.java`, and `HolidayRepository.java` — parse/normalize the pinned iCloud events and merge official status from `holiday-cn`.
- `app/src/main/java/com/clockmods/ui/CalendarLabelCarouselView.java` — fixed-height lunar/festival/solar-term upward carousel coordinated by the calendar grid.
- `app/src/pro/java/com/clockmods/pro/ProCalendarFragment.java` — dashboard lifecycle, binding, time, weather, selection, horizontal month paging, and accessibility.
- `app/src/pro/java/com/clockmods/pro/MonthPagerController.java` (or an equivalently scoped helper) — three-page month binding, gesture arbitration, snap/settle behavior, and shared navigation state if keeping this logic out of the fragment materially improves testability.
- `app/src/pro/java/com/clockmods/pro/ProMainActivity.java` and `ProPagerAdapter.java` — notify the live calendar page after settings are applied and explicitly dispatch calendar destination exit/re-entry so returning from another Pro page resets to today.
- `app/src/pro/res/layout/fragment_pro_calendar.xml` and `app/src/pro/res/layout-land/fragment_pro_calendar.xml` — portrait and landscape dashboard structures.
- `app/src/pro/res/drawable/*`, `app/src/pro/res/values/*`, and `app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml` — panels, semantic colors, dimensions, strings, and accessibility text.
- `app/src/pro/assets/calendar/cn_zh.ics` and its provenance/digest file — pinned primary festival and solar-term calendar from iCloud.
- `app/src/pro/assets/holidays/{2025,2026,2027}.json` and `app/src/pro/assets/licenses/holiday-cn-LICENSE.txt` — complementary official status data and required MIT notice.
- Existing tests under `app/src/test/java/com/clockmods/weather/`, `calendar/`, and `ui/` — extend with focused unit coverage.

### Tests and verification

1. Add a pure unit test proving a fresh basic cache is incompatible when detailed weather is enabled, triggers a forced fetch path, and becomes compatible after detail is stored. Also prove detailed-to-basic reuse and unchanged-settings reuse do not force requests.
2. Extend `QWeatherClientTest` with representative `/v7/weather/3d` JSON: validate request path/query, date mapping, min/max temperatures, day icon/text, non-200 handling, missing optional fields, and malformed/empty daily arrays.
3. Test forecast cache acceptance for exact location/source, rejection after TTL, rejection across local midnight, and rejection when any of today/tomorrow/day-after-tomorrow is absent.
4. Test ICS parsing with folded lines, language/value parameters, escaped text, unknown properties, exclusive multi-day `DTEND`, annual `RRULE` expansion, duplicate names, multiple distinct events on one date, malformed events, all 24 solar terms, and representative `春节`, `清明`, `谷雨`, `元宵节`, `（休）`, and `（班）` records. Validate the bundled snapshot's digest/provenance and bounded year coverage.
5. Test `holiday-cn` parsing for one `休` and one `班`, unknown years, malformed input, duplicate-date precedence, the upstream cross-year rule, and conflicts with ICS status. Validate all three bundled JSON files against required fields.
6. Extend `CalendarMonthTest` for 42 cells across month/year boundaries, today/selection identity, merged event/status attachment, short lunar labels, and the natural long lunar footer. Prove that event ordering is lunar first then all distinct ICS labels and that a date can retain multiple events.
7. Add focused carousel tests: no event means static lunar text with no scheduled frame; one or more events produces the complete sequence; transitions slide upward with stable bounds; callbacks stop on detach/pause; reduced-motion mode is static; and accessibility exposes all items without transition announcements. Add UI/Robolectric tests where practical for forecast mapping, selected footer updates, and saved month/selection restoration.
8. Add month-paging tests for left/next and right/previous direction, drag following, distance and velocity thresholds, snap-back, vertical-scroll rejection, tap preservation, repeated multi-month swipes, December/January transitions, leap-year clamping such as January 31 to February 29/28, adjacent-date taps, reduced motion, restored settled state, and parity between swipe/button/accessibility actions. Verify only the settled page runs label-carousel callbacks.
9. Add destination-lifecycle tests: browse to another month, switch Calendar -> Clock (and at least one other Pro destination) -> Calendar, then verify visible month, selected date, title, footer, three-page bindings, and active carousels all reset to today. Also prove that opening/closing Settings, permission dialogs, backgrounding/foregrounding, and configuration recreation while Calendar remains selected preserve the browsed month rather than falsely resetting it. Verify the reset uses the current app-zone date if midnight passes while Calendar is not selected.
10. Run `:app:testProDebugUnitTest`, then `:app:lintProDebug`, then `:app:assembleProDebug`. Also run relevant Modern/Compat unit/build tasks because the detailed-weather change is shared source.
11. Manual landscape acceptance: on a 16:9 device, verify the complete left/right composition, no overlap with Pro bottom navigation, correct baseline alignment, 7 x 6 grid, readable adjacent-month days, current-date green, and `休`/`班` badges from offline assets. Swipe repeatedly in both directions and verify each page follows the finger, settles to exactly one month, updates the title/footer, and never produces a blank page.
12. Manual portrait acceptance: verify stacked/scrollable modules, stable forecast columns, readable text at supported font scales, no clipped footer/title, and usable 48 dp month controls. Vertical scrolling must remain smooth while predominantly horizontal movement pages the calendar; tapping a date must not accidentally change months.
13. Manual return behavior: browse away from the current month, switch to Clock, then return to Calendar and verify it immediately shows and selects today. Repeat through another Pro page. Confirm that opening Settings and returning to the same Calendar destination does not reset the browsed month.
14. Detailed-weather acceptance: begin with weather enabled, detailed disabled, and a fresh basic cache; enable detailed and tap Apply. Without changing location or waiting for cache expiry, the clock keeps current weather visible, immediately enters refresh/loading behavior, and displays feels-like/humidity/wind detail after the request succeeds. Repeat for automatic and manual location modes and for MainActivity and ProClockFragment.
15. Forecast acceptance: with weather enabled, show today/tomorrow/day-after-tomorrow by `fxDate`; after midnight refresh/remap slots even if the prior cache age is short. With weather disabled, make no location/API request. With network unavailable, use valid cache and keep time/calendar functional.
16. Calendar-data acceptance: disable networking and browse the full range represented by the pinned ICS. Every available solar term and festival remains visible offline. A date with no event shows static lunar text; a date with one or more events vertically cycles through lunar text and every event without clipping or resizing the grid. For 2025-2027, compare sampled `休`/`班` results with both pinned sources; outside published arrangement coverage, show no fabricated badge.
17. Attribution acceptance: every page area displaying QWeather content visibly shows a legible standalone attribution linked to `https://www.qweather.com`.

- holiday-cn JSON schema: https://github.com/NateScarlet/holiday-cn/blob/master/schema.json
- holiday-cn raw annual files: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NateScarlet/holiday-cn/master/{year}.json
- holiday-cn releases for pinning: https://github.com/NateScarlet/holiday-cn/releases
- holiday-cn MIT license: https://github.com/NateScarlet/holiday-cn/blob/master/LICENSE

### Explicit exclusions

- Do not add a calendar page or navigation entry to Compat/Modern.
- Do not fetch iCloud or `holiday-cn` data at runtime or silently expand the bundled snapshot/range. Updating either source is an explicit build-time maintenance action with provenance and tests.
- Do not add events, reminders, calendar-provider integration, or editable holiday data.
- Do not make daily forecast depend on the detailed-weather switch.
- Do not rewrite the existing clock rendering or settings architecture beyond the shared cache-capability fix and the minimum settings-refresh notification needed by the Pro calendar page.
